record.original_question: Do there exist Fatou–Bieberbach domains which are not Runge? A Fatou–Bieberbach domain is a proper subdomain of C^2 which is biholomorphic to C^2 .

evidence.quote: Problem 10.1.1 Do there exist Fatou–Bieberbach domains which are not Runge? A Fatou–Bieberbach domain is a proper subdomain of C2 which is biholomorphic to C2 . -F. Forstneric, forstner@math.wisc.edu 10.2 The invariant set K + of a polynomial complex Henon map

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A Fatou–Bieberbach domain is a proper open subdomain Ω ⊊ ℂ² that is biholomorphic to ℂ². Such a domain Ω is called Runge if every holomorphic function on Ω can be approximated, uniformly on compact subsets of Ω, by polynomials on ℂ² (equivalently, by entire functions on ℂ²).

Question: Does there exist a Fatou–Bieberbach domain Ω ⊊ ℂ² which is not Runge in ℂ²?
artifact.status_search_result: The question was answered affirmatively by E. F. Wold, who constructed a Fatou–Bieberbach domain in ℂ² that is not Runge ("A Fatou–Bieberbach domain in ℂ² which is not Runge," Mathematische Annalen, 2008). Subsequent works have extended these constructions to Stein manifolds with the density property.

status_evidence.title: A Fatou–Bieberbach domain in C^2 which is not Runge
status_evidence.snippet: Wold constructs a Fatou–Bieberbach domain in C^2 which is not Runge.
status_evidence.claim: The existence question is resolved positively by Wold.

status_evidence.title: Non-Runge Fatou-Bieberbach Domains in Stein Manifolds with the Density Property
status_evidence.snippet: Studies existence of non-Runge Fatou-Bieberbach domains in Stein manifolds with the density property, citing prior resolution in C^2.
status_evidence.claim: Non-Runge Fatou–Bieberbach domains in C^2 are known to exist; further generalizations have been pursued.
